positioning: FoundarOS doesn't simply ask, 'Are you fundable?' It helps you understand what evidence your venture has today, what is missing, and what you need to prove next.

stages.name: IDEA STAGE
stages.description: I have an idea I'm exploring. I may still be working a 9–5 and haven't launched yet.
stages.focusMessage: Your biggest priority is not preparing a pitch deck. It is proving that your target customer experiences the problem strongly enough to seek a solution.

dimensions.label: Problem Strength
dimensions.why: A fundable case starts with a specific, costly or urgent problem experienced by a clearly identifiable customer.
strengthen: Interview people who experience the problem
Capture repeated pain points in their own words
Document how often the problem occurs
dimensions.proof: Five independent customer interviews that describe the same painful problem without prompting.

dimensions.label: Customer Definition
dimensions.why: A narrow first customer makes discovery, testing and early distribution practical.
strengthen: Describe their situation, behaviour and access point
List where you can reach them this month
dimensions.proof: A one-page ideal-customer profile validated in three conversations.

dimensions.label: Solution Clarity
dimensions.why: A clear solution hypothesis lets you test value before spending heavily on a full product.
strengthen: Create a sketch, demo or concierge test
Ask customers to compare it with their current alternative
dimensions.proof: A simple concept or prototype that target customers can react to.

dimensions.label: Market Potential
dimensions.why: Early market research shows whether the problem is common enough and valuable enough to support a venture.
dimensions.proof: A sourced bottom-up estimate for the first reachable market segment.

dimensions.label: Validation Evidence
dimensions.why: At idea stage, learning evidence matters more than revenue or a finished product.
dimensions.proof: A repeated problem pattern plus one concrete demand signal such as a follow-up, pilot interest or LOI.

dimensions.label: Business Model Potential
dimensions.why: You do not need a finished model yet, but you should have a testable view of who pays and why.
dimensions.proof: A target customer reacts to a specific offer and price rather than a hypothetical free solution.

dimensions.label: Founder Advantage
dimensions.why: Relevant insight, access or lived experience can reduce the risk of discovering and serving the right customer.
strengthen: Identify your unique access or expertise
Name the capability you still need
dimensions.proof: A concrete example of insight or access that another founder would find difficult to replicate.

dimensions.label: Funding Pathway
dimensions.why: The right next funding source depends on stage; many ideas should build evidence before seeking institutional capital.
strengthen: Estimate only what that milestone costs
Compare bootstrapping, grants, customers and equity
dimensions.proof: A milestone-based funding path that explains what evidence will be created before a larger raise.

questions.prompt: Who has the problem, and what makes it painful or urgent for them?
questions.help: Describe one specific person or organisation and the consequence of the problem.

questions.prompt: Who is the first customer you want to understand deeply?
questions.help: Be narrower than “everyone” — include their role, situation and context.

questions.prompt: How do they solve it today, and what would your solution change?
questions.help: Include workarounds, competitors and doing nothing.

questions.prompt: What have you done to understand the size and shape of this opportunity?

options.label: I have a sourced, bottom-up estimate for a reachable first market
I have researched the market and can explain a credible niche
I have seen broad market figures but not tested my assumptions
I have not researched the market yet

questions.prompt: What evidence have you collected that this problem is real and recurring?
questions.help: Customer quotes, observed behaviour and commitments are stronger than encouragement.

questions.prompt: Why do you believe they would pay, and what offer could you test first?
questions.help: You do not need revenue yet. State the value created and a testable offer.

questions.prompt: What makes you uniquely positioned to solve it?
questions.help: Consider lived experience, expertise, trust, distribution or unusual access.

questions.prompt: What access do you have to potential customers, and what proof could you build before seeking funding?
questions.help: Name real communities, relationships or channels and one milestone.

stages.name: VALIDATION STAGE
stages.description: I've started testing my idea, speaking to potential customers or developing an early prototype/MVP.
stages.nextMilestone: Move from early tests → repeatable demand evidence
stages.focusMessage: Your priority is turning encouraging feedback into observable behaviour: product use, pilots, commitments and willingness to pay.

dimensions.label: Problem Strength
dimensions.why: Strong validation begins with evidence that the problem is frequent, painful and prioritised.
dimensions.proof: Interview notes showing a repeated high-priority problem across a defined segment.

dimensions.label: Customer Definition
dimensions.why: A precise segment makes your test results interpretable and repeatable.
dimensions.proof: A consistent profile across the people who engage most strongly with the test.

dimensions.label: Solution Validation
dimensions.why: Solution evidence shows that customers can understand, use and value what you are building.
strengthen: Observe behaviour rather than asking hypotheticals
Track the same success measure across tests
dimensions.proof: Target users complete a meaningful task with the prototype and ask to continue.

dimensions.label: Market Validation
dimensions.why: Market validation tests whether demand exists beyond a small friendly circle.
dimensions.proof: Qualified prospects from a repeatable channel take the next step without personal favours.

dimensions.label: Business Model
dimensions.why: A testable price and payer hypothesis converts interest into commercial learning.
dimensions.proof: A real buyer accepts a price, paid pilot, deposit, pre-order or commercial conversation.

dimensions.label: Early Traction/Evidence
dimensions.why: Early traction is any meaningful behaviour that reduces uncertainty, not only revenue.
dimensions.proof: A growing set of users, pilots, LOIs, pre-orders or repeat engagements tied to the same use case.

dimensions.label: Founder Advantage
dimensions.why: The team must show the insight and learning speed to turn tests into a venture.
strengthen: Connect founder insight to test choices
dimensions.proof: A concrete founder advantage has enabled faster access, insight or execution.

dimensions.label: Funding Pathway
dimensions.why: Validation-stage capital should buy specific evidence, not simply more activity.
dimensions.proof: A milestone budget showing exactly which assumptions will be proven with the capital.

questions.prompt: What have customer conversations taught you about the frequency, urgency and cost of the problem?
questions.help: Share repeated patterns, not isolated praise.

questions.prompt: Which customer segment responds most strongly, and how has your definition changed through testing?
questions.help: Name the segment and the evidence behind your focus.

questions.prompt: What happens when target customers use or see your MVP, prototype or service test?

options.label: They complete a meaningful task, return or ask to continue
Several have tested it and given specific improvement feedback
People say they like the concept, but use is limited
I have not put a testable version in front of customers

questions.prompt: What evidence suggests demand exists beyond friends, family or your immediate network?
questions.help: Include channel tests, inbound interest or independent prospects.

questions.prompt: What have you learned about willingness to pay?

options.label: A target buyer has paid, placed a deposit or accepted a priced pilot
Buyers have discussed a specific price and buying process
I have asked hypothetically but not made a real offer
I have not tested price or who pays

questions.prompt: What is your strongest early traction or evidence signal today?
questions.help: Examples: active testers, repeat use, pilots, LOIs, pre-orders or referrals.

questions.prompt: How has your experience, access or team helped you learn or execute faster?
questions.help: Use one concrete example.

questions.prompt: What next milestone would funding help you prove, and what would it cost?
questions.help: Tie capital to an evidence milestone, not a list of activities.

stages.name: EARLY VENTURE
stages.description: I have launched and have some users, customers, pilots, revenue or other early traction.
stages.nextMilestone: Move from early traction → repeatable growth evidence
stages.focusMessage: Your priority is showing that early demand can become repeatable: acquisition, retention, revenue quality and a credible financial model.

dimensions.label: Problem & Solution
dimensions.why: A launched venture still needs a clear problem-solution narrative grounded in actual customer behaviour.
strengthen: Connect outcomes to the core problem
dimensions.proof: Customers consistently use the product for the intended high-value outcome.

dimensions.label: Market Validation
dimensions.why: Market evidence shows that demand extends across a coherent segment and reachable channels.
dimensions.proof: Qualified demand repeats across customers who share the same profile.

dimensions.label: Business Model
dimensions.why: A fundable business model connects pricing, delivery cost and repeatable customer value.
dimensions.proof: Customers pay a consistent price that supports a credible margin.

dimensions.label: Traction & Evidence
dimensions.why: Funders look for momentum supported by a consistent metric, not a collection of vanity numbers.
dimensions.proof: Three or more periods of improving traction in the metric that matters to the model.

dimensions.label: Customer/Revenue Evidence
dimensions.why: Customer quality, retention and revenue evidence show whether initial demand is durable.
dimensions.proof: Cohort or repeat-purchase evidence showing customers continue receiving value.

dimensions.label: Financial Readiness
dimensions.why: A simple, assumption-led model helps funders understand runway, unit economics and capital needs.
dimensions.proof: An updated model reconciled to actual revenue and costs with visible assumptions.

dimensions.label: Founder/Team Readiness
dimensions.why: The team must cover the capabilities required to deliver the next stage of growth.
dimensions.proof: A clear team plan tied to the next 12 months of execution.

dimensions.label: Funding Readiness
dimensions.why: A strong raise links a defined ask to measurable milestones and a coherent evidence-backed story.
strengthen: Tie use of funds to milestones
Prepare the core narrative and data room
dimensions.proof: A milestone-based ask supported by a model, traction data and clear use of funds.

questions.prompt: What customer outcome proves your launched solution addresses the intended problem?
questions.help: Use observed behaviour or results, not only your product description.

questions.prompt: Which customer segment and acquisition channel are producing the strongest signal?
questions.help: Include conversion or pipeline evidence where available.

questions.prompt: How do you make money today, and what have you learned about price and delivery cost?
questions.help: State actual pricing and cost evidence where possible.

questions.prompt: How consistently is your primary traction metric moving?

options.label: We have several periods of measurable growth in a defined metric
Traction is real but uneven or based on a short period
We have isolated users, pilots or revenue without a trend yet
We have launched but have little measurable engagement

questions.prompt: What do retention, repeat use, revenue or customer outcomes show?
questions.help: Use cohorts, repeat purchases, renewals, churn or specific outcomes.

questions.prompt: How current and evidence-based is your financial model?

options.label: It is updated with actuals, assumptions, runway and unit economics
We have a working model with some actual data
We have a rough budget but limited forecasting
We do not yet have a usable financial model

questions.prompt: What can the current team execute well, and which capability gap matters most next?
questions.help: Connect the gap to the next milestone.

questions.prompt: What are you raising, what will it fund, and which measurable milestones should it unlock?
questions.help: Include amount or range, runway and milestone outcomes.

stages.name: OPERATING & FUNDRAISING
stages.description: My business is operating and I am actively preparing to raise funding or apply for funding.
stages.nextMilestone: Move from operating evidence → investor or grant readiness
stages.focusMessage: Your priority is converting operating evidence into a precise funding case: growth metrics, financial model, ask, use of funds and diligence-ready documentation.

dimensions.label: Problem & Solution
dimensions.why: A concise problem-solution narrative keeps the funding case grounded in customer value.
dimensions.proof: Consistent customer outcomes that demonstrate material value.

dimensions.label: Market & Competitive Position
dimensions.why: Funders need to understand market scale, positioning and the venture's defensible wedge.
dimensions.proof: A sourced market model and customer-backed competitive positioning.

dimensions.label: Business Model
dimensions.why: A scalable model demonstrates how growth can translate into sustainable economics.
dimensions.proof: Reliable revenue and margin data showing how the model behaves as volume grows.

dimensions.label: Traction & Growth Evidence
dimensions.why: Meaningful growth evidence is central to a credible funding case.
dimensions.proof: A clean monthly KPI history with repeatable drivers and honest commentary.

dimensions.label: Financial Readiness
dimensions.why: A diligence-ready financial model connects historical performance, assumptions, runway and scenarios.
dimensions.proof: A three-year model tied to actuals with clear cash, runway and scenario logic.

dimensions.label: Funding Ask & Use of Funds
dimensions.why: A precise ask shows what capital buys, over what period, and how value will increase.
strengthen: Define the next financing inflection point
dimensions.proof: A board-ready use-of-funds plan linked to milestone, runway and hiring assumptions.

dimensions.label: Team & Execution Readiness
dimensions.why: Funders assess whether the team can deploy capital and deliver the proposed plan.
dimensions.proof: Named owners, execution cadence and a costed hiring plan for the funding period.

dimensions.label: Funding Documentation & Readiness
dimensions.why: Well-organised documents reduce friction and signal operational discipline during diligence.
dimensions.proof: A current pitch deck, model and indexed data room ready for controlled sharing.

questions.prompt: Which customer outcomes best demonstrate the value of your solution today?
questions.help: Use quantified outcomes, retention or repeat use where possible.

questions.prompt: How do you size the market and explain your competitive position or defensible wedge?
questions.help: Include sources, win/loss evidence and key alternatives.

questions.prompt: What do revenue quality, pricing, margins and unit economics show about the model?
questions.help: Distinguish recurring, contracted, pilot and one-off revenue.

questions.prompt: What are your core traction and growth metrics over the last 6–12 months?
questions.help: Include the trend, growth drivers, retention and pipeline quality.

questions.prompt: How diligence-ready are your financials and projections?

options.label: Historicals reconcile and a scenario-based model is current
We have a current model with a few gaps or untested assumptions
Financial records exist but the forward model is limited
Financials and projections are not yet ready for review

questions.prompt: What are you raising, how will it be allocated, and which milestones will it unlock?
questions.help: State amount, instrument if known, runway, major uses and measurable milestones.

questions.prompt: Why is this team equipped to execute the funded plan, and which hires are essential?
questions.help: Connect track record, ownership and hiring to the plan.

questions.prompt: What is ready for investor, lender, grant or accelerator review?

options.label: Pitch, model, cap table and an organised data room are current
Core documents exist and the data room is being completed
Some documents exist but material gaps remain
Funding documents are not yet assembled
